Flávio Bolsonaro Arrives in Florida After Fleeing Brazil Following Election Defeat

29 Oct 2026, 06:41 AM IST · GlobeWire Daily World Desk · Source: www.npr.org

Arrival and Statement

Flávio Bolsonaro, the defeated Brazilian presidential candidate, arrived at Miami-Opa Locka Executive Airport on Wednesday, October 28, 2026, after leaving Brazil amid multiple legal investigations. In his first public statement since departing, he declared himself Brazil's "president-elect" and accused President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva's government of political persecution and electoral fraud.

Border Crossing and Travel

Argentina's migration authority confirmed that Bolsonaro and his family crossed from Brazil into Argentina late Tuesday through the Tancredo Neves International Bridge. They entered with valid travel documentation and no legal impediments. The group then boarded a private flight to Guayaquil, Ecuador, before ultimately reaching Florida.

Legal Context

Bolsonaro faces multiple investigations in Brazil, including allegations of money laundering and tax evasion, which he denies. On Monday, Brazil's Supreme Court ordered him to surrender his passports within 24 hours and barred him from leaving the country. He is also under house arrest after being sentenced to 27 years in prison for plotting a coup following his 2022 electoral defeat.

Political Reactions

Former U.S. President Donald Trump has repeatedly cast doubt on Lula's victory, suggesting without evidence that the election was "rigged." President Lula criticized Bolsonaro's departure during his 81st birthday celebrations, calling it "shameful" and stating that Bolsonaro could have stayed to prove his innocence.

Uncertainties

While Bolsonaro claims he never intended to leave Brazil, the circumstances of his departure remain unclear. His campaign manager and lawyer previously stated they did not know his location. The specific legal implications of his arrival in the U.S. are also uncertain, though a senior U.S. administration official confirmed that the State Department issued visas to Bolsonaro and his family.

Verification

Readers can verify these facts through the official NPR report at https://www.npr.org/2026/10/27/nx-s1-6019678/bolsonaro-brazil-lula-election-trump and Argentina's migration authority statement on X.
